title: Modern Headless E-Commerce Architecture (Shopify Scale)
description: Design a high-scale headless e-commerce platform with multi-tenant storefronts, GraphQL APIs, distributed flash-sale inventory, and SAGA checkout.

data.text: Design a multi-tenant, headless e-commerce platform similar to Shopify or BigCommerce. The platform powers hundreds of thousands of independent merchant storefronts serving hundreds of millions of consumers. Headless architecture decouples frontend presentation layers (web, mobile, social commerce, smart devices) from core commerce backend engines (Catalog, Inventory, Cart, Checkout, and Order Fulfillment) via high-performance GraphQL and REST APIs. The platform must absorb extreme merchant flash sales without cross-tenant noisy neighbor impact while offering sub-100ms catalog browsing.

terms.definition: Separating the frontend presentation layer (Storefront UI built with Next.js/Hydrogen) from backend commerce engines via standardized GraphQL/REST APIs.
Partitioning merchant catalog, orders, and customer databases by `tenant_id` (Store ID) to ensure data isolation and prevent cross-store performance contention.
Streaming database row mutations (via Debezium/Kafka) from the primary transactional database directly into Elasticsearch search clusters in near-real-time.
Merging anonymous guest shopping carts (stored in browser cookies/Redis) with persistent customer accounts upon login without dropping items.
Shielding merchant checkout engines during sudden product drops by queueing buyers in an edge admission buffer.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Multi-Storefront Support: Headless APIs powering web, mobile apps, social commerce (Instagram/TikTok Shop), and POS terminals
Dynamic Product Catalog: Multi-variant items (size, color, material) with rich attributes and fast faceted search
High-Speed Cart: Persistent cart management supporting anonymous browsing, discount codes, and seamless login reconciliation
Flash-Sale Inventory Protection: Atomic stock decrement with zero overselling during limited product drops
Checkout & Payment SAGA: Multi-step checkout with address validation, tax calculation, and payment authorization
Merchant Admin Backoffice: Product creation, inventory replenishment, order fulfillment workflows, and analytics

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Multi-Tenant Scale: Support 1M+ active merchant stores; 50,000 global checkout transactions/sec during Black Friday
Storefront Browsing Latency: Sub-100ms P99 latency for catalog pages and search via edge caching
Isolation Guarantee: A flash sale on Store A must never degrade API latency or throughput for Store B (Noisy Neighbor isolation)
Data Consistency: Strict consistency for inventory allocation and payments; eventual consistency for reviews and search
Availability: 99.99% uptime for the storefront browsing and checkout APIs

data.text: Headless Storefronts run at the edge (Vercel / Cloudflare Workers) talking to a Storefront API Gateway (GraphQL). Multi-tenant isolation is enforced at the gateway and database sharding layers.

data.text: The sequence illustrates how an anonymous guest cart merges seamlessly upon customer sign-in, followed by atomic two-phase inventory reservation during checkout.

data.caption: Guest cart reconciliation on login, atomic inventory hold, and idempotent SAGA checkout flow
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Shopper as 👤 Shopper
    participant Store as 🌐 Headless Next.js Store
    participant GW as 🚪 GraphQL Gateway
    participant Cart as 🛒 Cart Service
    participant Redis as ⚡ Redis Cart/Stock
    participant Orch as ⚡ Checkout Orchestrator
    participant Pay as 💳 Payment Gateway
    participant Order as 📋 Order DB

    Shopper->>Store: Browse & Add Item (Guest Cookie: cart_anon_99)
    Store->>Cart: AddToCart(CartID: cart_anon_99, SKU: 881, Qty: 1)
    Cart->>Redis: HSET cart:anon_99 item:881 1

    Shopper->>Store: Logs into Account (UserID: user_55)
    Store->>Cart: POST /cart/merge {anonCartId: cart_anon_99, userId: user_55}
    Cart->>Redis: Merge guest items into user_55 persistent cart
    Cart-->>Store: Cart Merged (Total Items: 3)

    Shopper->>Store: Clicks "Checkout Now"
    Store->>GW: POST /checkout/submit (CartID, PaymentToken, IdemKey)
    GW->>Orch: Start Checkout SAGA

    Orch->>Redis: Atomic Lua Stock Decrement (SKU: 881, HoldTTL: 15m)
    alt Stock Available
        Redis-->>Orch: Stock Reserved
        Orch->>Pay: Authorize Payment ($120.00)
        Pay-->>Orch: Payment Authorized
        Orch->>Order: Create Order Record (Status: CONFIRMED)
        Orch->>Redis: DEL cart:user_55
        Orch-->>Store: 201 Created (Order #10948)
        Store-->>Shopper: Render Order Confirmation
    else Stock Sold Out
        Redis-->>Orch: Insufficient Stock
        Orch-->>Store: 409 Conflict (Item out of stock)
        Store-->>Shopper: "Sorry, this item just sold out!"
    end

faqs.question: How do you prevent the "Noisy Neighbor" problem in multi-tenant e-commerce?
faqs.answer: If Store A launches a viral celebrity sneaker drop with 500,000 req/sec, it must not degrade Store B. Implement tenant isolation: (1) Rate limits enforced per `tenant_id` at the API Gateway, (2) Dedicated database partitions or sharded Redis keys (`tenant:store_id:inventory`), and (3) Tiered worker pools where traffic surges are quarantined to dedicated autoscale clusters.

faqs.question: Why use GraphQL for Headless Commerce instead of standard REST?
faqs.answer: Headless storefronts need flexible data payloads: a mobile watch app needs only title and price, whereas a desktop product page needs full specs, variant tables, high-res image galleries, and review summaries. GraphQL eliminates over-fetching and under-fetching, enabling the frontend to request exact shapes in a single HTTP network round-trip.

faqs.question: How does Change Data Capture (CDC) keep product search in sync with database updates?
faqs.answer: When a merchant updates product titles or specs in the primary SQL database, Debezium captures transaction log updates and streams change events into Kafka. A search indexing consumer ingests the stream and updates Elasticsearch within 1-2 seconds, decoupling the transactional write database from search query loads.

faqs.question: How are cart sessions stored for millions of unauthenticated guest users?
faqs.answer: Anonymous guest carts are stored in a distributed Redis cluster keyed by a signed UUID cookie (`cart:anon_uuid`) with a 30-day sliding TTL. This avoids consuming expensive relational database rows for casual window shoppers who never complete checkout.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Headless commerce decouples edge storefront presentation from backend transactional commerce engines
Multi-tenant data sharding by Store ID protects against noisy neighbor performance interference
GraphQL Federation aggregates Catalog, Cart, and Inventory into unified, performant frontend queries
Redis atomic Lua scripts execute zero-overselling inventory holds during high-traffic flash sales
Change Data Capture (Debezium + Kafka) keeps Elasticsearch product indexes updated without direct DB coupling
data.takeaway: Modern headless commerce platforms combine edge-rendered Jamstack storefronts with federated GraphQL APIs, backing multi-tenant stores with isolated, fault-tolerant transactional microservices.
